faqs.q: How long should I stay in a company before switching jobs?
faqs.a: Many employers like to see at least a year or two in a role, as it shows commitment and gives you real achievements to talk about. Several very short stints in a row can raise questions in interviews, though a single early move for a clear reason, such as a better role or a difficult workplace, is usually easy to explain.

faqs.q: How much salary hike can I expect when switching jobs in India?
faqs.a: There is no fixed figure; the hike depends on your industry, role, skills, experience and how much demand there is for your profile. Research market pay for similar roles, compare the full package rather than just the fixed salary, and negotiate based on what you bring.

faqs.q: Should I resign before getting a new job offer?
faqs.a: It is usually safer to have a written offer in hand before resigning, so you are not left without income during a long search. If you need to leave sooner for health or workplace reasons, make sure you have enough savings to cover several months of expenses.

faqs.q: What is a notice period and can it be shortened?
faqs.a: A notice period is the time you must keep working after resigning, as set out in your appointment letter or employment contract. Some employers agree to release you early, or let you or your new employer pay in place of the remaining notice, so check your contract and discuss it openly with HR.
